# CXNM - Standard - IOS - D - Restrictions Corporate

Hardening for supervised corporate iPhones and iPads: no manually installed profiles or developer apps, no apps from outside the App Store, untrusted TLS certificates automatically rejected, no erasing via Settings, a lock screen without Control Center, notification history, Today view and Siri, and Activation Lock only with a bypass code stored by Intune.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | iOS/iPadOS |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | UniFy iOS/iPadOS Baseline v1.2 (CIS Apple iOS/iPadOS 26 Benchmark v1.0.0, L1) — merged from SC - Device Restrictions, Device Security, Device Pairing, Lock Screen, Safari Browser, Web-App-Store (EU) and Apple Intelligence & Siri - Corporate; IntuneAdmin — Disable Web Distribution App Installation EU. Values corrected where UniFy uses `_false` as 'do not enforce' |
| File | [`Baseline_IOS_D_Restrictions_Corporate.json`](Baseline_IOS_D_Restrictions_Corporate.json) |

> Deliberately **not** included: allowpasswordautofill=false (UniFy Corporate) — that also disables passkeys and password managers; forceauthenticationbeforeautofill is used instead. iCloud backup and iCloud Drive off (UniFy Corporate) — an organisational decision about where data may be stored, not hardening; managed apps already do not sync to iCloud via CXNM - Standard - IOS - D - Data Protection. Blocking Bluetooth, NFC, hotspot and VPN changes (Connectivity Controls, L2) — breaks car kits, payment cards and working from home. Siri fully off — only Siri on the lock screen is off. Host pairing (Finder/iTunes) is handled by the enrollment profile (iTunesPairingMode disallow), not by this policy. allowopenfromunmanagedtomanaged not blocked: otherwise a photo from the Photos app can no longer be shared in Outlook or Teams — the same trade-off as with allowedInboundDataTransferSources in App Protection. Control Center off on the lock screen also means: no flashlight without unlocking. Corrections to UniFy: forceautomaticdateandtime is false there (= not enforced), true here. Activation Lock: UniFy blocks it (false); allowed here (true), because a supervised device then has theft protection while Intune keeps the bypass code (device action 'Disable Activation Lock'). Before rollout, check that Intune shows a bypass code for a test device; without that code a returned device with a personal Apple Account cannot be reused — in that case choose false. This policy shares the top-level group com.apple.applicationaccess with Data Protection but does not set any key twice; iOS merges restriction payloads.
